name: Speculative decoding: draft-model proposal pass
arithmetic_intensity: The draft pass reads the draft model's weights for k tokens' worth of positions at once. With a draft of size N_d, flops = 2*k*N_d against bytes = 2*N_d (weights) + small activations, giving AI ~ k flop/byte - the batch-k of a batched decode GEMM. So the draft pass is memory-bound exactly like decode_gemm, at effective batch k; it is cheap only because N_d is a small fraction of N_target. It also runs the full KV-cache attention and norm/sample work for k positions, so its overhead is not purely the GEMMs. The design condition for the whole scheme is that the draft's per-step latency must stay below the target model's single-token latency, which is why DeepMind's speculative sampling argues parallel scoring of a short continuation costs about the same as sampling one target token (arXiv 2302.01318).
scales_with: draft_k (number of speculative positions - AI = k, and this is the entire lever)
draft_model_size (N_d relative to N_target sets the overhead fraction)
draft_depth or tree width (for tree/multi-candidate variants, which multiply draft work)
context_length (draft KV attention grows with context like any attention)
workarounds: Use the cheapest possible draft: an n-gram / prompt-lookup drafter needs no weights at all and costs only a KV/memory lookup
Early-exit the draft model at a chosen layer depth rather than running a full separate model
Run the draft pass on a smaller colocated device, or concurrently with the target model's previous step's tail
Tree / multi-candidate drafting with a verification-aware acceptance test to raise accepted tokens per draft pass
notes: Design consequence: speculative decoding is a bandwidth trade, not a compute trade. It can only pay when the target model is memory-bound (low batch, small weights) - which is exactly why its benefit shrinks as batch grows and CI/engines expose it as a latency optimization rather than a throughput one. Hardware implication: the win needs a device that can hold both models and re-read the target weights less often; a part too small to co-reside simply cannot use it. The accounting trap is that draft cost is real work, so speedup is bounded by (1 + draft_cost/target_cost) and by the acceptance rate - quoting the speedup without the acceptance rate and k is not a complete claim.
